title: The income quintile rows of Figure 1 and Table A1 carry each other's labels
published: [[Below 20th income percentile]], [[20th-40th income percentile]], [[40th-60th income percentile]], [[60th-80th income percentile]], [[Above 80th income percentile]]
corrected: [[20th-40th income percentile]], [[40th-60th income percentile]], [[60th-80th income percentile]], [[Above 80th income percentile]], [[Below 20th income percentile]]
note:
The deposited script builds the grouping factor with its levels typed in alphabetical order and its labels typed in substantive order, so each income row is printed under the label belonging to the group before it and the lowest quintile is printed as the highest. Every other block in the same call lines up, because only the income levels sort differently under the two orders. The direction is not a matter of interpretation: income_quintile is a self-describing character variable whose five categories partition the deposited household income measure, and the row the article prints as the bottom quintile reports N = 1,038, which is the size of the second quintile; the bottom quintile has 804.

The changed artifact is the five labels alone. No estimate, standard error or sample size moves, and no conclusion turns on it: the article's claim about income is that the groups did not diverge widely, which holds under either labelling. The maintained rewrite prints the labels the data supports, which is why its income rows disagree with the published ones in the ground truth.
